findings.body:
Rule 7/A4. statusmodel/cost.go:79-93 emits the decisions line metered with USD 0 whenever any decision record exists, even with no usage block, and nothing ever sets jev.Usage.CostUSD, so every local run with a decision shows 'decisions $0.00'. Cloud: runs.cost_usd is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and cloudStatusDoc (status.ts:481-492) / status_model.go:647 turn any number into a metered 'AI Gateway logs' line, so a run before its first cost sync or with telemetry 'unavailable: …' (cost_source, unread on the status path) shows 'Workers AI $0.00'. Fix: emit the decisions line metered only when a record carries a measured cost, and make the cloud line unmetered unless cost_source is 'gateway'; teach P3's generator a metered-zero/no-usage decision and an unsynced cloud record.
evidence: internal/statusmodel/cost.go:79-93; internal/jev/jev.go:185; cloudflare/migrations/0002_runs.sql:16; cloudflare/src/status.ts:481-492; internal/cli/status_model.go:647
findings.title: Cost still prints a fabricated $0.00: decisions line and cloud default 0

findings.body:
Rule 3/A2. runCompleted (build.go:735-744) treats any run_finished not prefixed 'failed:' as completed, so an operator-stopped run with open ticks reads phase done, merge done, verdict healthy, attention [] and still shows an ETA (live: `ticfac status epic-hn6 --json` for run_08f5…, stopped 15:59 with 2/35 ticks open). A completed local run waiting on its PR (phase merge, not alive) reads red 'stopped' (verdict.go:90 exempts only done/cancelled). A failed run gets no dead-run wait (build.go:785 runTerminal), so the frame says 'needs you: nothing' beside '● stopped' though a person must resume it. nextStepOf (pipeline.go:620) promises 'the run will retry' on a dead/failed run. Fix the lifecycle/verdict/needs-you for stopped, failed and completed-awaiting-merge runs, hide ETA on ended runs, and add tests for each.
evidence: internal/statusmodel/build.go:735-744, :785; internal/statusmodel/verdict.go:90; internal/statusmodel/pipeline.go:620; `ticfac status epic-hn6 --json` → phase done, verdict healthy, attention [] for a hard-stopped run
findings.title: Ended runs get a false verdict, phase and needs-you (stopped reads done/healthy)

findings.body:
A3. attemptDiff (report.go:286) reads only while the attempt branch exists, and sweepTick deletes it on close (dispatch.go:3667), so every merged tick's drill-in says 'diff not read'. Under `watch epic-<id>` a tick's row comes from the prior run that closed it, but the report reader is bound to the CURRENT run id (status_model.go:529) and is handed the prior run's per-run attempt number, which yields 'report not read' or another dispatch's report when the numbers collide. Gate evidence is the newest run's only (build.go:217). Record diff stats durably at collect (or diff the merged commit), key reports by (run, tick, attempt), merge gate evidence per tick across runs, and test a drill-in on a closed prior-run tick.
evidence: internal/statusmodel/report.go:286, :48-64; internal/reconcile/dispatch.go:3667; internal/cli/status_model.go:529; internal/statusmodel/build.go:217; internal/statusmodel/epic.go header
findings.title: Drill-in shows no diff, report or gate evidence for settled and prior-run ticks

findings.body:
Regression from watch's raw-mode keys. term.MakeRaw (watch_keys.go:283) disables ISIG, so Ctrl-C arrives as a key; watch.go:991-997 returns interrupted() → 1 (or ExitHeld) without cancelling the context. attachRun (run.go:618) and runCloudAttach (run_cloud.go:80) map 1→5 'detached' only when ctx.Err()!=nil, so a person who presses Ctrl-C or q on `ticfac run` gets exit 1 and 'the watch was interrupted' while the run keeps going: the misread tick 8v3 fixed. Tests mask it (run_test swaps attach for a context cancel; TestWatchOnATerminalTakesKeys asserts 1 for q on a live run). Fix: make a key interrupt indistinguishable from a cancel to attach callers (cancel or return the running class), and test the real attach with a key.
evidence: internal/cli/watch_keys.go:283; internal/cli/watch.go:991-997, :861-871; internal/cli/run.go:611-628; internal/cli/run_cloud.go:80
findings.title: Ctrl-C/q on a terminal under `ticfac run` exits 1, not 5 'detached'

findings.body:
A5/rule 8 ('two renderers, they cannot disagree'). For cloud runs the Worker composes its own doc (status.ts:431-495: no health, progress, workers or ci, waves null, phase from run.state, one cost line) while `ticfac watch run_<hex>` builds the full Go model, so the same cloud run shows a verdict, table and per-source cost in the terminal and a bare state chip on the phone. On the same pushed document the phone prints 'degraded: degraded: …' (phone.ts:612 prefixes a summary verdict.go:117-131 already prefixes) and 'stopped: ' for an empty summary, and omits the workers panel, CI line and elapsed. Fix: render cloud runs on the phone from the same model (push or serve the Go-built doc), share the verdict wording, and add a cross-renderer test over the degraded and stopped goldens.
evidence: cloudflare/src/status.ts:431-495; cloudflare/src/phone.ts:612; internal/statusmodel/verdict.go:117-131; internal/cli/watch_view.go:241
findings.title: Phone page shows a different model for cloud runs and garbles verdicts

findings.body:
RESULT-{378,3gk,7uv,hn6,ltg,oro,r5i,v16}.md sit at the repository root on the integration branch; the epic's PR would land them on main, which #172 cleaned of exactly this ('a worker's report is a run's transport, not a file of the project'). report_merge.go says existing reports 'stay until somebody removes them'. And #169's guard does not cover the base-fold-through-resolve path: ab0cdab4 (2026-10-04, after #169 was on the branch) rewrote RESULT-hn6.md. Remove the eight files from epic/hn6 and route the base-fold resolve merge through keepReportsOut.
evidence: git ls-tree HEAD --name-only | grep RESULT; git diff ab0cdab4^1 ab0cdab4 --stat -- RESULT-hn6.md; internal/reconcile/report_merge.go:1-30
findings.title: Epic branch carries 8 worker RESULT-*.md reports to main's root

findings.body:
ulw/qxj add --run-id run_<hex> so the store opens, but settle then calls addressForSettlement, which requires the attempt's executor state on the machine running settle; a cloud attempt's state lives in the factory container, so the command the header prints refuses with 'this host holds no state … nothing to release'. Tests compare strings only. Needs a factory-side release or a different named command for cloud holds.
evidence: internal/reconcile/settle.go:494-499; internal/reconcile/settle_command.go:18
findings.title: A cloud attempt hold's printed settle command still cannot release it

findings.body:
acceptTrackerEdits treats every BLOCKED/no-commits report with an acceptable tracker edit as the delivery and closes the tick, without checking the edit answers the blocking question; only the standing orders' always-ask class guards it. A 'BLOCKED — acceptance ambiguous' report proposing a clarifying edit to its own tick closes with no code. Tests cover only the yjq shape.
evidence: internal/reconcile/tracker_edits.go:157-200
findings.title: l89 closes any blocked tick that carries any acceptable tracker edit

findings.body:
adoptInheritedFindings reads every run's checkpoint on the integration branch (other epics' included) before filtering by epic; decodeRecord disallows unknown fields and any error aborts Run. A factory-written checkpoint newer than the local binary, or one corrupt record, stops every run of the epic at boot. Each boot also asks ClaimHolder serially per non-terminal sibling.
evidence: internal/reconcile/inherit.go:50-75; internal/reconcile/reconcile.go:1976
findings.title: One unreadable sibling checkpoint fails every boot of the epic (d23)

findings.body:
